To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pupillary light response to blue light was preserved in both genetically confirmed ADOA patients with c.983A>G or c.2708-2711delTTA mutations despite severe visual loss, and that the ipRGSs are not affected in ADOA.

despite severe optic neuropathy and visual loss, the pupillary light responses to blue light of 300 cd/m 2 were preserved in both c.983A > G and c.2708_271 1delTTAG autosomal dominant optic neuropathy.

the pupillary light response to isoluminant blue and red light is preserved in ADOA, despite the severe visual loss, and is not related to the thickness of the peripapillary retina, ganglion cell layer or age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel method to evaluate the pupillary light response in patients with ADOA, and the results suggest that the melanopsin-based photoreception is spared in this disorder, despite severe visual loss.
the development and validation of a new method for the detection of melanopsin containing, intrinsically light sensitive retinal ganglion cell (ipRGC).
the development of a new, non-invasive diagnostic test, based on the pupillary light response, to detect the earliest stages of the disease, and to monitor the effect of new therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in ADOA, the melanopsin containing ipRGCs and their pupillary post-illuminancy response are spared, despite the severe optic neuropathy and the poor BCVA.
the ipRGSs are spared in both the c.983 A > G or the c. 2708_2712delTTAG mutations.
the ipRGGs are preserved in genetically-confirmed ADOA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ipRGSs are spared in the ADOAs, and the PLR is preserved.
the melanopsin-based PLR to blue, high intensity light is preserved in ADOA, despite the severe visual impairment and optic atrophy, and is not related to the severity of the disease.
the ipRGS are spared in AOA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PLR is preserved in ADOA, despite the severe visual impairment, and this is not related to age or retinal thickness.
the PLR can serve as a biomarker for the integrity of the melanopsin containing retinal ganglion cell system, and that it is preserved in ADOA.
the ipRGSs may be spared in ADOAs and the PLR to blue, red, or white light of high luminosity may be used as a biomarker of the ipRGC survival in this condition.
